::: callout-important
## Instructions

- Pick one of the following tasks and work as a group, guided by the group navigator.

- While this week focusses on Gaussian models and the tasks below are for you to practice them, you should also get summary measures and plot the data, so that you familiarise yourself with the data sets and you keep practising skills learned in earlier weeks.
:::

::: callout-note
## Task A: Mixean Basque Voice Onset Time

- [Data docs](https://uoelel.github.io/qml-data/data/egurtzegi2020/eu_vot.html).

- Read the `egurtzegi2020/eu_vot.csv` data.

- Filter the data to include only aspirated consonants.

- Answer the following question using a Gaussian model: what is the mean and SD of aspirated VOT in Mixean Basque?

- Write a results paragraph.
:::

::: callout-note
## Task B: Shallow morphological parsing (RT)

- [Data docs](https://uoelel.github.io/qml-data/data/song2020/shallow.html).

- Read the `song2020/shallow.csv` data.
  Familiarise yourself with the study (<https://uoelel.github.io/qml-data/data/song2020/shallow.html>).

- Filter the data to include only L2 data from critical trials.

- Answer the following question using a Gaussian model: what is the mean and SD of reaction times in L2 participants?

- Write a results paragraph.
:::

::: callout-note
## Task C: Reading fixation times (eye-tracking)

- [Data docs](https://uoelel.github.io/qml-data/data/berzak2025/fix-dur.html).

- Read `berzak2025/fix-dur.csv`.

- Answer the following question using a Gaussian model: what is the mean and SD of fixation durations in the data set?

- Write a results paragraph.

- Now run another model but with only 5 participants (sample 5 random participants from the data set).
  What happens to the posterior distributions of the mean and SD?
:::
